A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PhyWorldBench study and contain 35 pages, including Appendices A–T. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the text, mathematics, tables and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of 12 video-generation models using 12,600 generated videos, alongside CAP evaluator experiments, ablations and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, including the human evaluations in Table 3 and the evaluator and supplementary results in the appendices.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction procedure and CAP's two-stage description-and-assessment prompting remain unchanged, including the prompts in Appendix K.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1,050 prompts covering fundamental, composite and anti-physics scenarios. The supplementary abrupt-change, complexity and failure-case coverage is also unchanged.

E2.justification: The same video generators, MLLM evaluators, CAP variants and model-scale comparators participate in corresponding comparisons. Updated citations do not introduce evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: Evaluation settings remain identical, including SA/PC criteria, eight-frame evaluator input, three-annotator majority voting, the reported 80/20 fine-tuning split and supplementary sampling procedures.

E4.justification: CAP ablations, prompt comparisons, model-scale analysis, static-scene rationalization, abrupt-change and complexity tests, and qualitative failure examples are retained without revision.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version introduces additional run or seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests relative to the other.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, CAP retains SA/PC ROC-AUC values of 80.3/75.1, and Pika 2.0 retains its overall Both score of 0.262.

T1.justification: The binary SA/PC definitions and aggregation rules are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The claims about benchmark breadth, anti-physics evaluation, zero-shot CAP assessment, model physics deficiencies and physics-enhanced prompting retain the same meaning and scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning rationalization, training-data imitation and cinematic bias remain unchanged, as do Appendix I's coverage limitations and Appendix D's evaluator failure modes.

D1.justification: The page-10 reproducibility statement changes promised code/data release to completed release. This clarifies release status: Appendices J and T already document available resources in v2 and remain unchanged, so no newly available resource or implementation detail is established.

R1.justification: Research positioning and the cited benchmark membership remain unchanged. Bibliographic revisions associated with VideoPhy, DEVIL, Physics-IQ, WISA and Morpheus update authors, titles, publication details or dates without changing their discussed roles.

P1.justification: Edits are confined to bibliography entries, corresponding in-text citations, the reproducibility paragraph and the arXiv version/date stamp. The narrative and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Reference and citation updates cause localized text reflow and spacing changes, particularly on page 10. Figures and tables retain their designs, captions, contents and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves the contradiction between page 10's promised release and the existing availability disclosures in Appendices J and T. This provides a limited improvement in clarity and internal consistency; the scientific methods, evidence and limitations remain unchanged.
